# Temple Scroll Column 39 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 39 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**39:1** You shall construct a moat surrounding the temple, outside the outer court, to prevent sudden entry into My temple.

**39:2** The moat shall be one hundred cubits wide and of great depth.

**39:3** Between the moat and the outer court there shall be a space of seven cubits, and trees shall be planted in it.

**39:4** You shall construct a parapet along the moat so that no person falls into it.

**39:5** They shall not defile My temple by entering it suddenly while in a state of impurity.

**39:6** They shall sanctify My temple and hold My sanctuary in reverence, for I dwell among them.

**39:7** You shall construct latrines outside the temple city, to the northwest, at a suitable distance from the city.

**39:8** They shall go out to them — roofed structures with pits beneath — into which the waste shall descend.

**39:9** These shall not be visible from the temple city at any distance.

**39:10** No person shall go out to them on the Sabbath; the distance shall be three thousand cubits from the temple city.

**39:11** You shall establish three places to the east of the city, separated from one another, for the various categories of impurity.

**39:12** These places shall accommodate those with skin diseases, those with discharges, and men who have experienced a seminal emission.

**39:13** They shall not enter the temple city until their purification is complete; on the day of their purification they shall wash and be clean.

**39:14** They shall bring their prescribed offerings, and the priest shall declare them clean.

**39:15** Thereafter they may enter the temple city; no impure person shall be found within it.

**39:16** For it is the city of the temple; I, the LORD, have hallowed it and established My name upon it; it shall be holy forever.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 39 covers three defensive and purity features: the moat (vv. 1-5), latrines (vv. 7-10), and quarantine zones (vv. 11-14). The Sabbath latrine prohibition (v. 10) connects to broader sectarian halakhah found in the Damascus Document (CD 10:10-11). The 3,000-cubit distance exceeds the standard 2,000-cubit Sabbath limit.*
